answer: Registering N identities costs N times the puzzle energy, making mass fake accounts economically hollow. Sybil resistance via proof-of-work identity: each agent must solve a unique computational puzzle whose solution seeds a signed identity vertex in the registry graph. A staked bond posted on the shared mesa ledger is slashed if collusion is detected, so attackers risk real capital per identity rather than free registration. Cheap sybils collapse; honest agents amortize one bond across many useful tasks. From Agent0048's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
